# Instantiation and Field Access

```metel
struct Point {
    x: f64,
    y: f64,
}

extend Point {
    fun at(x: f64, y: f64) -> Point {
        Point { x = x, y = y }
    }
}

fun main() -> i64 {
    let p := Point::at(1.0, 2.0);
    let x := p.x;
    return x as i64;
}
```

The brace literal builds a value directly from its fields. It is legal only inside its
type's own `extend` blocks, [covered below](#spec.declarations.structs.privileged-representation-construction.legality-1);
everywhere else the same value is built with
[call-syntax construction](#spec.declarations.structs.call-syntax-construction.legality-1),
`Point(x = 1.0, y = 2.0)`.

When a local variable has the same name as a field, the `= value` part can be omitted
([**shorthand field init**](#spec.declarations.structs.instantiation-and-field-access.legality-1)):

```metel
struct Point {
    x: f64,
    y: f64,
}

extend Point {
    fun at(x: f64, y: f64) -> Point {
        Point { x, y }
    }
}

fun main() -> i64 {
    return Point::at(1.0, 2.0).x as i64;
}
```

Shorthand and explicit fields may be mixed freely within one literal.

Zero-field structs [may omit braces entirely](#spec.declarations.structs.instantiation-and-field-access.legality-2).
These two forms are [equivalent](#spec.declarations.structs.instantiation-and-field-access.dynamics-2):

```metel
struct Empty {}

let a := Empty;
let b := Empty {};
```

<details>
<summary>Formal rules</summary>

##### Legality Rule {#spec.declarations.structs.instantiation-and-field-access.legality-1}

A struct-literal field initializer is `ident`, optionally followed by `= expr`. When `=
expr` is present, `ident` names the field and `expr` its value. When omitted, `ident` must
name both the field and a local binding in scope at the literal (shorthand/punning field
init). Shorthand and explicit fields may be freely mixed within one struct literal.

##### Dynamic Semantics {#spec.declarations.structs.instantiation-and-field-access.dynamics-1}

A shorthand field `ident` in a struct literal evaluates identically to the explicit form
`ident = ident`: the field takes the value of the local binding named `ident` that is in
scope at the literal.

##### Legality Rule {#spec.declarations.structs.instantiation-and-field-access.legality-2}

A zero-field struct may be constructed either as its bare type name or with empty braces.

##### Dynamic Semantics {#spec.declarations.structs.instantiation-and-field-access.dynamics-2}

For a zero-field struct, the bare and empty-brace constructor forms evaluate to the same
struct value.

##### Legality Rule {#spec.declarations.structs.instantiation-and-field-access.legality-3}

A struct with fields cannot omit its constructor fields; its bare type name is resolved as a
name rather than as a constructor expression.

## Call-syntax construction

Ordinary construction is [a plain call](#spec.declarations.structs.call-syntax-construction.legality-1):
`Point(x = 1.0, y = 2.0)`, keyword or positional, resolved by ordinary name lookup. A
module's type and value declarations share one namespace, so this call can never be
ambiguous between constructing `Point` and invoking a same-named function — at most one
declaration named `Point` can exist in scope, so the call means whichever one it is.

```metel
struct Point {
    x: f64,
    y: f64,
}

fun main() -> i64 {
    let p := Point(x = 1.0, y = 2.0);
    return p.x as i64;
}
```

<details>
<summary>Formal rules</summary>

##### Legality Rule {#spec.declarations.structs.call-syntax-construction.legality-1}

A call `T(args)` where `T` names a struct or enum (not a function) is a construction
expression, resolved by the same positional/keyword argument rules as a function call.
Every field is supplied exactly once; there is no field-init shorthand/punning in call
position. A module's `struct`/`enum` declarations and its `fun`/`let`/`var` declarations
share one namespace: declaring a type and a value under the same name in the same scope
is an ordinary redeclaration error, so `T(args)` is never ambiguous between construction
and a function call.

<!-- rfc.py:last_reviewed ccec8913745b4209ac504134cce36cef0780ad27 -->

<!-- rfc.py:origins:end -->

##### Dynamic Semantics {#spec.declarations.structs.call-syntax-construction.dynamics-1}

Construction arguments evaluate left to right as written, then the canonical
construction operation runs on the complete, ordered field row. Construction specifies
neither heap allocation nor a fresh runtime identity.

<!-- rfc.py:last_reviewed ccec8913745b4209ac504134cce36cef0780ad27 -->

## Privileged representation construction

The nominal brace literal above this page's shorthand-field-init rule is
[restricted to a single privileged use](#spec.declarations.structs.privileged-representation-construction.legality-1)
once call-syntax construction exists: anywhere inside an `extend` block of its own type,
inherent or aspect impl, `Point { x = 1, y = 2 }` builds the value directly from its
fields, invoking no constructor and implying no validation. Elsewhere, a struct is
constructed only through call syntax. An enum variant's brace literal,
`Shape::Circle { radius = 1.0 }`, is restricted the same way, to the enum's own `extend`
blocks.

```metel
struct Point { x: i64, y: i64 }

extend Point {
    fun origin() -> Point { Point { x = 0, y = 0 } }
    fun shifted(self, dx: i64) -> Point { Point { x = self.x + dx, y = self.y } }
}

fun main() {
    let p := Point::origin().shifted(3);
    let q := Point(x = 1, y = 2);   // outside Point's own extend blocks: call form
    assert(p.x + q.y == 5);
}
```

<details>
<summary>Formal rules</summary>

##### Legality Rule {#spec.declarations.structs.privileged-representation-construction.legality-1}

An explicit field-list or whole-row (`Self { ..fields }`) brace construction of a struct,
or of an enum variant, is legal only inside the body of an `extend` block whose target is
that struct or that enum, and targets only that type (`Self` or its explicit type name).
It initializes every field exactly once; a missing, duplicate, or extra field is an
error. Elsewhere in the declaring module, and in every other module, construction uses
the call syntax. A literal that initializes no field (`Empty {}`, `Flag::On {}`) is the
same value as the bare form and is not restricted.
